content.intro: In this lesson, you will study error handling in vbscript as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 32 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: Error Handling in VBScript matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Intermediate VBScript code benefits from predictable object lifetime, focused error handling, and small reusable procedures. For 'Error Handling in VBScript', choose the simplest construct that matches the requirement, document any COM dependency, and avoid suppressing errors across unrelated statements. A legacy script can be improved without changing externally visible behavior by adding focused checks first.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: Runtime errors; The On Error Resume Next statement; The On Error GoTo 0 statement; The Err object; Checking Err.Number; Clearing and reporting errors; Limiting the scope of suppressed errors. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Error Handling in VBScript
content_blocks.code:
<%
On Error Resume Next
Err.Clear
Dim number
number = CLng("not-a-number")
If Err.Number <> 0 Then
  Call LogError(Err.Number, "numeric conversion")
  Err.Clear
  Response.Write "The request could not be processed."
End If
On Error GoTo 0
%>
content_blocks.expected_output: A generic error message is shown; `LogError` is an application-defined, protected server-side routine.

content_blocks.text: Use a local Classic ASP page. Change one value or statement at a time, capture the observed output, and check at least one empty, malformed, or boundary value. content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of error handling in vbscript. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small, reviewable demonstration of error handling in vbscript using synthetic data. Include at least one of these syllabus concepts: Runtime errors. State the expected result first, then add one invalid or boundary case and explain how your program should behave.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.
